content.title: Nested Routes and Layouts
content.hook: Imagine three account screens all have the same structure:
content.context:
```text
Account header
Account navigation
-------------------
Current account screen
```

You could repeat that shell in three separate screens. But then a change to the account header means changing three places.

A nested route structure gives the shared shell a home of its own.
goals: Understand how a shared application shell can stay visible while a child route changes inside it.

content.title: Parent and child
content.text:
Use this simplified route tree:

```text
/account
  ├── /account/profile
  └── /account/security
```

The parent route owns the shared account layout.

The child route owns the content area.

content.question:
The user moves from `/account/profile` to `/account/security`.

What is the most useful mental model?

options.text: The account shell must be rewritten by both screens.
The shared parent can remain while the child content changes.
The browser deletes the parent UI permanently.
The child route becomes the entire application.

feedback.correct: Nested routes are useful because shared structure can remain while the currently selected child content changes.
feedback.incorrect: Nested routes are useful because shared structure can remain while the currently selected child content changes.

content.title: A route tree
content.text:

feedback.correct: A layout boundary should own what is genuinely shared by the routes beneath it.
